text: For a discrete-time system, when is a fixed point stable according to the eigenvalues of its Jacobian J?
choices: When all eigenvalues satisfy Re(lambda_k) < 0 (left half-plane)
When all eigenvalues satisfy |lambda_k| < 1 (inside the unit circle)
When all eigenvalues satisfy |lambda_k| > 1 (outside the unit circle)
When the determinant of the Jacobian is exactly zero
explanation: In discrete time a fixed point is stable iff every Jacobian eigenvalue lies strictly inside the unit circle, |lambda_k| < 1 (equivalently rho(J) < 1). Re(lambda_k) < 0 (option 0) is the continuous-time criterion; |lambda| > 1 is instability; det(J) = 0 is a degenerate, non-hyperbolic case.
